chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who pushed another man onto a man, causing him to kill him, he said:
The diyyah is upon the one who fell upon the man and killed him, for the heirs of the slain.
He said: And the one who was pushed may recover the diyyah from the one who pushed him.
He said: And if anything happens to the one who was pushed, then that too is upon the one who pushed him.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.ٱلدَّافِعِ: the one who did the pushing
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةُ: blood money; the prescribed financial compensation for unlawful killing

ai.seo_question: Who is liable for diyyah if someone pushes a person onto another and the latter dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on liability when one person pushes another, causing the death of a third person. The immediate killer is responsible for the diyyah to the heirs of the slain, while the person who was pushed may then seek reimbursement from the one who initiated the push. It also establishes that any harm suffered by the pushed person is likewise the responsibility of the pusher.
